# BB00071: Ziyarat for the Point and his Letters of the Living {.unnumbered}

## Part 1: “When thou desirest to visit the Point or…” {.unnumbered}

In the name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy

When thou desirest to visit the Point or one of the Letters of the Living, thou must refine thyself to the utmost degree of refinement such that if thou shouldst know there is even one superfluous hair upon thy body, it would be unfitting at that time. And thou must wear thy most pure garments, not the most splendid thereof, such that if thou wearest an old shirt that is pure, good, refined and clean to the extent that thou knowest not even a speck of dust the size of a mosquito's wing is upon it; for if thou knowest of such, it would be unfitting. When thou findest thyself in that most glorious state and supreme refinement, place upon thy finger a ring of red carnelian, which is the sign upon that path before thy glorious Lord and the means of attaining unto God upon the throne of glorification.

Then pray two rak'ahs in [...] and say in the first [...] after the takbir that God may teach thee:

> "O God, our Lord, the All-Merciful! God beareth witness that there is no God but Him, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting. His is the dominion and the kingdom, then the might and the power, then the strength and the sovereignty, then the force and authority. He giveth life and causeth death, then causeth death and giveth life, and verily He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not, and the King Who passeth not away, and the Just One Who wrongeth not, and the Sovereign Who changeth not, and the Single One from Whose grasp escapeth nothing whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. He createth what He willeth by His command. Verily He is the All-Knowing, the Mighty, the Great."

> "O God, our Lord, the All-Merciful! Say: He is the One, the Single, the Eternal Being, the Everlasting Existence, the Self-Sufficient, the Divine Being sanctified and relied upon, Who begetteth not nor is begotten, and there is none like unto Him."

Then in the second rak'ah do as in the first, and at the point of glorification say three times:

> "Glory be to God, the Lord of might and majesty! Glory be to God, the Lord of beauty and countenance! Glory be to God, the Lord of power and perfection!"

Then with hands outstretched say:

> "Glory be unto Thee, O God! There is no God but Thee, and Thou hast no partner. Thine is the creation and the command, from before and after. Thou givest life and causeth death, then causeth death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. In Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily Thou art powerful over all things. Grant us, O God, every good thing which Thy knowledge encompasseth."

In thy sitting position say:

> "God beareth witness that there is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Best Beloved. And I verily testify before God and all things that the Seven Letters are the Gate of God in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and what lieth between them, and we all believe in Him. Verily God will send His blessings upon the Letters of Unity according to what He hath ordained from His presence at all times, before time and after time. He is the Protector, the Best Beloved."

Then if thy place be empty of anyone save those with whom God hath permitted thee to recline, prostrate thyself and say in thy prostration "I seek forgiveness of God, our Lord, the All-Merciful" seven times in the morning and the evening. Then be silent and walk with dignity and composure until thou seekest permission at the gate with this luminous method:

Glory be unto Thee, O God, my God! Thou hast ever been existent before all things, and a being with all things, and established above all things, and existing after all things. Nothing escapeth Thy knowledge whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them, and nothing in the kingdom of command or creation or below them can frustrate Thee. I testify before Thee and all things that Thou hast ever been and wilt ever be One God, Single, Alone, Self-Sufficient, Ever-Living, Self-Subsisting, All-Holy, Just, eternally holy and everlasting, self-subsisting. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any helper in what Thou hast fashioned. All are within Thy grasp and in the right hand of Thy will. Thou givest permission to whom Thou pleasest, how Thou pleasest, for what Thou pleasest, and Thou deniest whom Thou pleasest, how Thou pleasest, for what Thou pleasest. Thou art not questioned about what Thou doest, but all shall be questioned about what they do.

Therefore it behooveth thee, if thou art possessed of knowledge and art able to read and art capable thereof, not to neglect purification and refinement, for these are among the attributes of man. And remember God with what floweth from thy tongue in a state of tranquility and complete turning to God. When thou reachest the gate before the hand of God, prostrate thyself and say:

> "There is no God but God, the Ever-Living, the Ever-Living. There is no God but God, the Just, the Just. There is no God but God, the True, the True. There is no God but God, the Lord, the Lord. There is no God but God, the Single, the Single. God, God is my Lord and I associate none with Him."

For this sufficeth thee in place of all prayers. And thou shouldst speak these words standing after rising from thy prostration. Then present thyself before God and recite the verse of prayer. Then say:

> "Verily the Most Splendid Glory is from God, Who is none other than He, the Possessor of the Most Exalted Similitude. Upon thee, O Most Exalted Tree, in the hereafter and the former times."

This sufficeth thee as a grace from God and a bounty from His presence in His Book. Verily, He is the Self-Sufficient, the Beloved.

But if thou art knowledgeable of what God hath revealed and art capable of communing with God and desirest to take delight in the melodies of the birds of heaven, then stand if thou art in the presence of God, otherwise sit in whatever position thou art able to maintain stability. For God is nearer to thee than thy very self, and the Manifestations of His Cause are nearer to thee than thy very self.

And say there: O Thou Who art the Most Splendid above all splendor! O Thou Who art the Most Exalted above all exaltation! O Thou Who art the Most Elevated above all elevation! ## Part 2: “I beseech Thee by the Divine Point…” {.unnumbered}

I beseech Thee by the Divine Point and then by the Letters of the Living, that Thou send Thy blessings upon the Tree of Thy love and whatsoever is in it and upon it, and that Thou reckon without the Tree of Thy love and whatsoever is in it and upon it, for verily Thy knowledge is never absent from anything in the heavens or on the earth or whatsoever is between them, and nothing can frustrate Thee in the kingdom of command and creation and whatsoever is beneath them, and verily Thou art the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful, the Exalted.
